rules.statement: Express personal style rather than prescribing a single correct taste; the system should feel curated, enabling, and individual.
Pair editorial inspiration with a clear commercial or service action; neither glossy mood nor transactional UI should dominate the whole experience.
Present expertise with warmth and accessibility. Avoid snobbery, gatekeeping, or language that makes good design sound unattainable.
Use supplied official wordmark or compact elephant artwork. Preserve proportions, orientation, and internal spacing; never redraw or synthesize the mark.
Maintain clear space around the logo equal to at least the compact elephant mark's height and keep it visually separate from promotions and photography.
Do not stretch, rotate, outline, bevel, shadow, pattern-fill, animate by distortion, or place the logo on visually noisy detail.
Use heritage green as the signature anchor for primary actions, major brand fields, or key headings; support it with white, warm neutrals, and natural material colors.
Reserve sale red for discounts, markdowns, and time-sensitive transaction states; do not use it as a general decorative accent.
Use powder blue sparingly for badges, calm secondary fields, and selected campaign support. It must not replace heritage green as the enduring brand anchor.
Use the editorial serif for emotionally led display lines, room stories, and inspiration. Do not use it for dense controls, prices, specifications, or navigation.
Use the interface sans for navigation, headings, labels, product names, actions, and compact informational text.
Use the reading sans for paragraphs and extended product or service copy, with comfortable line height and restrained tracking.
Limit uppercase and wide tracking to navigation, compact labels, action text, and selected section headings; never set paragraphs or long headlines in uppercase.
Use square or nearly square controls, cards, image frames, and panels. Rounded containers are exceptional, not a default visual language.
Primary actions use a solid heritage-green rectangular field, white uppercase interface text, generous horizontal padding, and no visible corner radius.
Editorial secondary actions may be text-led uppercase links with measured tracking and a simple underline or directional cue.
Use generous outer margins and section separation so imagery, products, and typography can breathe; avoid dense dashboard-like packing.
Lead emotional stories with a composed room or outdoor setting, then move into product, material, and service detail.
Rooms should feel layered, intentional, and livable: collected objects, tactile materials, natural light, and believable negative space without sterile minimalism or visual clutter.
Show specific material character such as linen, velvet, aged wood, lacquer, brass, raffia, stone, ceramic, and woven fibers; avoid vague glossy luxury surfaces.

When depicting a real product, preserve its geometry, materials, scale, finish, color, and functional details. Generated interpretation must be labeled and cannot substitute for a verified catalog image.
Catalog cutouts use a centered straight-on or three-quarter view on white or very light neutral gray, with consistent scale and soft natural grounding.
Use people sparingly and contextually to demonstrate living, hosting, consultation, or scale. The room and design story remain primary; avoid fashion-campaign posing.
Write with warm expertise: concrete design language, confident guidance, short inviting actions, and respect for the customer's own taste.
Avoid empty prestige phrases such as 'unparalleled luxury,' 'elevate your lifestyle,' or 'timeless elegance' without a specific product, material, provenance, or design idea.
Prices, offers, inventory, shipping promises, product specifications, and promotion deadlines must come from a current authoritative data source at generation time.
Treat seasonal palettes, campaign slogans, discount codes, and offer art as replaceable inputs. They may inform a current execution but must never mutate core brand rules or tokens.
Critical headlines, offers, product data, and actions must remain selectable or otherwise semantically available; text embedded in imagery requires an equivalent accessible text layer.
Meet WCAG 2.2 AA contrast for essential text and controls, adding a quiet solid field or tonal overlay when photography cannot provide dependable contrast.
All interactive elements require visible focus, keyboard operation, meaningful labels, non-color state cues, and touch targets of at least 44 by 44 pixels.
Use assets only for purposes permitted by their rights record. Public-site references in this package are evidence, not proof of production reuse or model-upload permission.
Interpret brand semantics independently of any specific renderer, model provider, framework, agent, or authoring application; adapters translate these rules downstream.
